description: Fix the explored one-crash known-hole recovery schedule and compare complete serialized command content at two actual commitments for the same origin/instance. This is fresh formal execution, not reuse of exploration.

harness.description: Actual full formation and recovery handlers with typed codecs, one stopped participant and explicitly pending original Commit.
semantic_changes: Bounded empty-state initialization and in-memory peer streams under serial ownership.
Peer 0 stops after initial commit support; other messages follow the declared finite dispatch schedule.
Direct recovery entry abbreviates watcher waiting after an observed missing-slot premise.

legality.derivation: Reuse the empty-state and actual codec helpers after independently checking this prefix. Origin 2 creates a same-key conflicting proposal to peers 0/4, left pending. Origin 1 proposes the target to peers 0/2; real differing PreAccept replies lead to real Accepts, matching replies and checked origin COMMITTED. Peer 0 then stops and all suffix broadcasters mark it not alive; no further handler or reply from 0 is used. Origin 1 retains its preference order, skips failed 0, and sends its later slot 1 to peers 2/3. On link 1->3 the already-sent Commit for slot 0 is decoded first and retained pending; the next decoded PreAccept for slot 1 is dispatched. Production replicaListener creates independent enqueue goroutines per decoded RPC and run selects separate message-type channels, so byte order does not force Commit dispatch before PreAccept or recovery. The scheduler can finitely delay that enqueue/dispatch through the bounded suffix. This is not arbitrary reordering of a FIFO handler queue. Slot 1 receipt establishes crtInstance[1]=1 while slot 0 remains absent, exactly the watcher missing-slot predicate. The direct recovery entry abbreviates time until the watcher queues recovery; it introduces no fabricated value. Replica 3 uses preferred peers 2/4, sends actual Prepare, processes their actual decoded replies with its self report, and follows actual generated PreAccept/Accept messages to attain a second commitment. All pending messages, including the original Commit, are retained; no target protocol state or generated payload is replaced. The first coordinator remains live. Observation and buffers have one test-goroutine owner; the test ends without shutdown mutation.
legality.applicability: Finite controlled asynchronous schedule, not a timing guarantee. Bounded arrays and omitted networking/execution goroutines do not alter the exercised handler transitions. Per-type pending work is explicit and all used link bytes are decoded in order.
unresolved: The scheduler abstracts watcher waiting and enqueue delay; no quantitative probability or deadline claim.
Final application and causal isolation are outside this check.
alternatives: A faster Commit enqueue/dispatch would give a different history and is not an obligation on this asynchronous schedule.
Recovery output is not replaced by an expected NOOP; the driver observes target-generated command batches.

grounding.derivation: The captured system declares replicated state-machine protocols and the executable configures tolerance of F crash failures. EPaxos coordinates a command batch by origin/instance identity. Its commit paths mark that identity decided, and execution consumes its commands. handleCommit refuses to replace already committed instances; recovery skips local committed entries with commands and prioritizes committed/accepted evidence before proposing anew. These interfaces and guards establish decision preservation as an applicable responsibility: a later recovery must not decide a different command batch for an already decided identity. This safety duty is not derived from whether the experiment differs or from assuming that the implemented recovery/quorum formulas satisfy it.
grounding.applicability: Static five-member thrifty crash-stop configuration, F=2, one actual stopped participant after initial quorum commitment, finite asynchronous delay of intact messages and legal instance recovery. Distinct nonfailed replicas observe commitment of the same origin/instance.
unresolved: Specific causal contribution of each local defect is not isolated.
No completed client/application divergence is asserted.
alternatives: Delayed Commit could teach the original decision if dispatched earlier, but safety must hold for permitted finite delayed dispatch.
Retained attributes and preaccepted recovery alternatives may protect other histories; the selected history exercises the actual combined recovery path.

observable_properties.description: Complete command batch content in the second actual commitment equals the earlier committed batch for the same origin/instance.

uncertainties: No application or client endpoint measurement.
No individual-cause attribution among recovery self-report, codec and phase behavior.
